title: Masks
summary: Shine a spotlight on a picture with a mask layer, then tween the mask to sweep the light across it.

steps.title: Welcome
steps.text:
In this lesson you will make a spotlight: a circle on a mask layer that lets a picture show through only where it is, then sweeps across it.

The document is ready: the colorful Picture layer, and an empty Spotlight layer above it. Click Next to begin.

steps.title: Pick the Oval tool
steps.text: Press O, or click the Oval tool in the toolbox.

steps.title: Draw the spotlight
steps.text:
Make sure the Spotlight layer is the current one, with the pencil beside its name; click its name if not. Then hold Shift and drag a circle on the left of the stage.

Its color doesn't matter: a mask only uses the shape of its fills.

steps.title: Make it a mask
steps.text:
Right-click the Spotlight layer's name and choose Mask.

The Picture layer below becomes masked by it, and both layers are locked.

steps.title: See the result
steps.text:
The picture now shows only through the circle, and the rest of the stage is empty.

On the stage a mask masks only while its layer is locked. Unlocked, it shows its own art and the picture whole, so you can edit it. Exports always mask.

steps.title: Unlock the mask
steps.text: Click the lock icon on the Spotlight layer's row to unlock it, so you can animate the circle. Leave the Picture layer locked.

steps.title: Go to frame 48
steps.text: Click frame 48 of the Spotlight layer, the last frame. At 24 frames per second that is two seconds in.

steps.title: Insert a keyframe
steps.text: Press F6, or choose Insert > Timeline > Keyframe. Frame 48 starts with a copy of the circle.

steps.title: Move the spotlight
steps.text: Press V for the Selection tool. Double-click the circle to select all of it, then drag it to the right side of the stage.

steps.title: Tween the mask
steps.text: Click any frame between 1 and 47 on the Spotlight layer, then choose Insert > Shape Tween, or right-click the frame and choose Shape Tween.

steps.title: Lock it again
steps.text: Click the lock icon on the Spotlight row again, so the mask masks on the stage.

steps.title: Play it
steps.text: Press Enter, or click the play button in the timeline header. The spotlight sweeps across and reveals the picture as it goes.

steps.title: Well done
steps.text:
You made a mask layer, saw how locking it shows the result, and tweened the mask to make a moving spotlight.

To mask more layers with the same mask, drag them in just under it, or set their type to Masked in Layer Properties. Help > Tutorials has more lessons, such as Rigging with layer parenting.
